chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from him that he said:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Indeed, the rising by night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech."
He said: "It is a man's rising from his bed, intending by it the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not intending by it other than Him."

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night, the time of nocturnal worship
key_terms.غَيْرَهُ: other than Him, indicating exclusive sincerity for Allah
key_terms.فِرَاشِهِ: his bed, indicating leaving comfort for devotion
key_terms.قِيَامُ: standing or rising, here meaning getting up for worship
key_terms.نَاشِئَةَ: rising or getting up, here referring to rising in the night
key_terms.وَجْهَ: the Face, meaning Allah's good pleasure and nearness in this context

ai.seo_question: What does "Indeed, the rising by night is firmer in tread and more upright in speech" mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration explains the verse as referring to a person rising from bed in the night solely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It highlights the sincerity of intention in night worship and presents night rising as an act of pure devotion directed only to Him.
